summary.title: Anti-Self-Distillation for Reasoning RL via Pointwise Mutual Information

details: On-policy self-distillation (teacher = student conditioned on privileged context such as a verified solution + correctness feedback) gives inconsistent or negative gains on math reasoning RL.

Diagnosis: the per-token self-distillation signal equals the conditional pointwise mutual information PMI(y_t; c | x, y_<t), so it rewards 'shortcut' tokens already implied by the privileged solution and penalizes deliberation tokens (Wait, Let, Maybe) that drive multi-step search.
AntiSD: replace descent on the student-teacher divergence with ascent on it, flipping the per-token advantage sign so deliberation tokens are rewarded and shortcut tokens penalized.

Ascending Jensen-Shannon (rather than reverse KL) yields advantage -phi(u_t) = -(softplus(u_t) - log 2)/2, which is automatically capped on the over-sampled deliberation side and linear on the shortcut side.

A Schmitt-trigger entropy gate switches the term off when median teacher per-token entropy collapses (so the log-ratio degenerates), making AntiSD a drop-in replacement for default self-distillation at no extra cost.
Five models: Qwen3-8B, Qwen3-4B-Instruct-2507, Olmo-3-7B-Instruct, Olmo-3-7B-Think, Qwen3-30B-A3B (4B-30B, incl. an MoE).
Training on DAPO-Math-17k for 200 on-policy steps; code probe on Dolci-RLZero.

Privileged context c = verified solution (a correct rollout from the group, else the dataset reference) concatenated with a correctness feedback string (binary for math, 'passes N of M tests' for code); student rollout re-scored under this context.
GRPO with group-normalized sequence advantage; additive combination A_{i,t} = A_i^seq - lambda * sg[phi(u_t)], lambda_max = 0.5.
AdamW, lr 1e-6, 32 problems x 8 rollouts per step, 32K max sequence length, clip 0.2, no reference-KL penalty; verl framework on H20 GPUs.
Gate auto-calibration: 5 warmup steps at lambda=0 give H_warm; deactivate below tau_down = 0.93*H_warm, reactivate at H_warm; the 0.93 multiplier shared across all models.
avg@32 on AIME 2024/2025/2026 and HMMT 2025; avg@4 on MinervaMath; pass@k curves on HMMT 2025; avg@10 on HumanEval+ / MBPP+.
Metrics reported at each run's best-Avg checkpoint, plus 'speedup' = GRPO's best-Avg step divided by the step at which a method first reaches that accuracy.
Baselines: untrained base, +GRPO (lambda=0), +SD (default self-distillation with delta_t = +u_t).

Ablations: reverse-KL ascent vs JSD; gate off and tau_down in {0.90, 0.93, 0.95}; additive vs multiplicative composition; teacher- vs student-perplexity gate signal; a 'No-teacher' variant removing privileged context entirely.
Continual experiment: resume GRPO@200 checkpoint and run 50 further AntiSD steps with recalibrated gate.

Lemmas: reverse-KL gradient identity giving delta_t = +u_t; PMI characterization of u_t via Bayes; telescoping of u_t to trajectory PMI, making the shaping potential-based (optimal-policy invariant per Ng et al.).
JSD f-divergence generator derivative f'(e^{-u}) = -phi(u); phi strictly increasing, sign-preserving, and bounded below by -(1/2)log 2 (unbounded above).

key_findings.finding: The per-token signal of on-policy self-distillation is conditional PMI between the next token and the privileged context, which structurally rewards shortcut tokens and suppresses deliberation tokens.
key_findings.evidence: Gradient identity shows the KL-descent per-token advantage is exactly u_t = log pi_T - log pi_S = PMI(y_t; c | x, y_<t); measuring u_t on Qwen3-4B-IT-2507 AIME-25 rollouts yields two off-diagonal lobes in a (pi_S, pi_T) heatmap: strongly positive u_t on tokens like 'Given', 'holds', 'succeeds' and strongly negative (down to u_t <= -20) on 'Wait', 'Let', 'Maybe', 'Alternatively'; the argument extends to any convex f-divergence.

key_findings.finding: Reversing the sign (AntiSD) both accelerates and improves reasoning RL over a strong GRPO baseline, while default self-distillation underperforms it on every model.
key_findings.evidence: Across five 4B-30B models, AntiSD reaches GRPO's best average in 2-10x fewer steps and gains +2.1 to +11.5 average points (e.g. Qwen3-8B 65.7 vs GRPO 57.4 vs SD 30.6; Qwen3-4B-IT-2507 62.8 vs 51.3 vs 45.9); 4 of 5 models win on every individual benchmark (lone -0.6 pp on Minerva for Olmo3-7B-TK).

key_findings.finding: The gain comes from expanded problem coverage rather than concentrating mass on already-solved problems.
key_findings.evidence: HMMT 2025 pass@k at peak checkpoints: on Qwen3-8B AntiSD leads GRPO by ~13 points at k=1 and still ~7-10 points at k=32, with non-converging curves at high k.

key_findings.finding: AntiSD's benefit depends specifically on the privileged-context differential, not on generic shaping of student log-probabilities.
key_findings.evidence: The 'No-teacher' variant (signal a function of student log-prob alone) collapses within ~70 steps on all three tested models, a self-reinforcement collapse; in contrast AntiSD keeps entropy in a stable middle band while default SD's entropy either collapses to ~0.1 nats (Qwen3-4B, run terminates at step ~80 with length pinned at the 32K cap) or inflates past 1 nat (Olmo3-7B-IT).
